author: human8e
text:
Human8e Ltd | Applied cryptographer, protocol review | REMOTE (worldwide) | Contract, fixed fee

We're an early-stage UK company building a mobile application, funded by its founder (just me), which is why the scope below is deliberately narrow.

I'm looking for an applied cryptographer to review a protocol specification before it ships. It is small and specific: three messages, two parties, signature-based, using hardware-backed keys on both iOS and Android. It uses standard primitives only (ECDSA over P-256, SHA-256) and invents no new cryptography; the question is how they are combined. The specification is written and frozen, with test vectors and the generator that produces them.

What I want is a competent second opinion on whether it is sound: six specific questions answered in writing. Not an open-ended audit or a penetration test. The person I'm looking for has either published on protocol security or reviews protocols professionally; being good with crypto libraries isn't quite the same thing.

One piece of contract work, not a role. Under a short mutual NDA.

Email clive@human8e.com by Sunday 4 October with a short summary of the protocol analysis you've done, and I'll send scope, timing and what I'd need from you.

author: cbzehner
text:
Fazeshift | Senior Software Engineer | San Francisco, CA | ONSITE 5 days | Full-time | $200k–$235k + equity

I’m Chris, VP Engineering at Fazeshift. Accounts receivable sounds boring until you look under the hood: it sits at the intersection of money, business relationships, old and new software systems, and a huge amount of repetitive human work.

We build AI agents that actually do that work — billing, collections, payments, and cash application. Since 2024, we’ve grown revenue 12x and eight unicorns now run their AR on Fazeshift. We’re nine engineers plus our Founder/CTO and me.

The interesting engineering constraint is that *we intentionally aren’t the system of record*. Our agents take real actions across customers’ ERPs, banks, billing systems, and other infrastructure. A timeout doesn’t necessarily mean a write failed; webhooks can arrive late or twice; blindly retrying can be exactly the wrong thing to do.

That creates some fun problems:

* How do you let agents take consequential actions safely — with the right permissions, auditability, idempotency, durable execution, and human intervention?
* How do you build one coherent product across systems you don’t control?
* How should an engineering team work when coding agents can handle meaningful chunks of implementation, debugging, testing, and exploration?

We’re especially interested in engineers whose development workflow has already materially changed because of coding agents. We use them heavily, often in parallel, but generated code is still your code. Judgment, debugging, systems thinking, taste, and understanding what actually shipped matter a lot here.

We’re looking for 5+ years of experience, strong TypeScript/full-stack skills, and real production ownership. No fintech experience needed.

Stack: TypeScript/Next.js, tRPC, Prisma/MySQL/PlanetScale, Inngest, AWS.

I read every application myself. Email chris.zehner@fazeshift.com with HN in the subject, your résumé/LinkedIn/GitHub, and a few sentences about one concrete way coding agents have changed how you build software — including how you verify their work.

author: cpeterson42
text:
Thunder Compute (YC S24) | C++ Systems, Infrastructure, BizOps | San Francisco (Onsite) | Full-time | https://www.thundercompute.com

We're building the VMware for GPUs. Most GPUs in the cloud sit idle a lot of the time because they're bolted to one machine over PCIe. We decouple them.

Our virtualization layer is a userspace shim, loaded through LD_PRELOAD, that intercepts CUDA calls and ships them over the network to a host with a physical GPU somewhere else in the data center. Workloads run unchanged. When a process goes idle, the GPU detaches and gets reassigned, and reattaches in tens of milliseconds when it's needed again. Think Ceph for GPUs: the GPU becomes a network resource a cluster-wide scheduler can pool and pack.

The hard part is making that fast. We're within ~10% of native on most AI workloads, and it lets us serve ~1.8x more users on the same fleet. We run it in production as our own GPU cloud and sell it to enterprises with underutilized fleets.

Team is from Citadel Securities, Aquatic, Old Mission, AWS, and Bain. Series A, $17.5M raised from Matrix and Y Combinator.

Expect to be reading minified code to find where state lives and analyzing network logs to understand undocumented APIs. You will figure out how AI products work and build the prototyping and automation to maintain our software inventory.

To apply:
Send an email to eric+hn@sidekicklabs.com with the role in the subject. Include a PDF of your resume, a quick sentence or two about a tough technical problem you've solved recently, and links to your GitHub, personal site, and/or LinkedIn.

I'm Eric, VP of Technology, and I will personally read every email sent to the HN subaddress. You can view my background here: https://www.linkedin.com/in/three-two-one
